§11.2.1 Bars and Histograms

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-bars-and-histograms · charts types

✅ Normative

A bar chart MUST be rendered as a chart table with one value per bar: one row per category, one column per series. A histogram is a bar chart whose category is the bin: a bin the axis does not label MUST still get its row, labeled by its axis value, and a labeled position with no bar MUST hold 0.

  • A single series gives a two-column table — see the full example in Values and Tolerances§11.1.4.
  • Grouped bars give one column per legend series — see the full example in Labels§11.1.2.
  • Horizontal bars change nothing: the category axis simply runs vertically, and rows follow it top to bottom.
  • A highlighted or average bar (EU average, shaded behind the rest) is an ordinary row. An average line is reference ink and adds nothing to the table (see Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3).

Histogram bins

Printed bin labels are copied verbatim, catch-alls included (> 15000). When the axis labels only every other bin, the unlabeled bins still exist: each gets a row labeled by its axis value — 2000 between the ticks 1500 and 2500 on an axis labeled every $1 000. A bin that no printed calibration reaches is not locatable (see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1).

✅ Sample — catastrophe-review-2025_p4

Bins every $500, labels every $1 000, a printed catch-all, and one labeled position (1500) with no bar. Full coverage is 29 rows: 1500 holds 0; the unlabeled bins are labeled by their axis values (2000, 3000 …); every count is an estimate against the 20-unit grid. The catch-all keeps its printed space (> 15000). The value axis title heads the single value column; the category axis title heads the label column.

Progress and target bars

A goal statement with a single bar, its current value marked on it and the target at its right end, is a one-row bar chart, not a chart type of its own. Its chart table MUST hold the current value, the target and the axis end-points: the bar's meaning is relative to its scale, and 7 against 8 or 42% against 50% is only legible with that scale kept.

✅ Sample — goal cards with progress bars

Three goal cards separated by rules. Each bar marks its current value (40%, 7, 42%, each with the year 2024 beneath it) against a scale from its start (0%, 0) to its target (100% with 2030 Target, 8 with 2025 Target). The rows follow the axis: start, current value, target. The third card's scale end-points fall below the crop and are not shown, so its table holds only the current value.
